title: The rocky road to quiescence: compaction and quenching of quasar host galaxies at z ∼ 2
question: What are the intrinsic dust morphology, CO line morphology and kinematics, and star formation properties of z ~ 2 quasar host galaxies, and how do they relate to galaxy compaction and quenching?

data.sensitivity: 7 to 93 uJy beam^-1 (continuum rms with natural weighting)

what.value: Ancillary photometric data for SED fitting of lensed quasars

evidence.quote: The SED fitting follows a similar procedure described by (cite: Stacey:2018a) and uses ancillary data listed therein.

what.value: Lens model parameters (slope, ellipticity, position angle, and nearby galaxy parameters) for PG 1115+080 and WFI J2033-4723

evidence.quote: Robust lens models have been produced for PG 1115+080 and WFI J2033$-$4723, based on higher quality optical imaging of the quasars and extended arcs as part of the H$_0$ Lenses in COSMOGRAIL’s Wellspring (H0LiCOW) project (cite: Chen:2019; Rusu:2020).

recipe.goal: Calibrate raw visibilities, self-calibrate, subtract continuum, and create lens-plane images and line profiles
recipe.method: ALMA pipeline calibration in CASA, phase self-calibration on line-free windows (for 4 targets), linear continuum subtraction in visibility plane, CLEAN deconvolution with natural weighting, and single Gaussian fitting to integrated line profiles

recipe.goal: Visibility-plane gravitational lens modelling and pixellated source reconstruction
recipe.method: Simultaneous optimisation of singular power-law ellipsoid lens mass distribution with external shear and pixellated source surface brightness directly on visibilities
key_parameters: isothermal profile zeta = 2 (for 5 targets); fixed literature slope/ellipticity/PA for PG 1115+080 and WFI J2033-4723
maximum baseline < 300 m and 3 velocity channels for WFI J2033-4723 and SDSS J0924+0219 line cubes
assumptions: Smooth singular power-law ellipsoid mass distribution with external shear; SIS for nearby perturbers in WFI J2033-4723

recipe.goal: Measure intrinsic source sizes (R_eff), Sersic indices, and lensing magnifications
recipe.method: Fit 2D Sersic profiles to 100 noise realisations of reconstructed continuum and integrated CO line sources using basin-hopping optimisation; compute mean magnification by masking source pixels below SNR of 4
key_parameters: 100 noise realisations; SNR >= 4 mask for magnification; Sersic index n fixed to continuum value (1.0) for SDSS J0924+0219 and WFI J2033-4723 CO lines
assumptions: Additional +/- 10% uncertainty added to sizes where isothermal slope was assumed to account for empirical scatter in lens mass profile slope

recipe.goal: Fit SEDs to derive dust temperatures, FIR/IR luminosities, SFRs, SFR surface densities, Eddington limits, and dust masses
recipe.method: MCMC fitting of an optically thick modified blackbody (plus warm dust component for 2 sources and radio power-law where applicable) to sub-mm and ancillary photometry, followed by analytical conversions to L_FIR, L_IR, SFR, Sigma_SFR, and M_dust
key_parameters: nu_0 = 3 THz (100 um) where tau = 1; beta = 2 fixed for HS 0810+2554; H1413+117 photometry > 300 GHz scaled by 0.8 for neighbour confusion
assumptions: Salpeter IMF with Kennicutt (1998) conversion SFR = L_IR / (5.8e9 L_sun); dust mass opacity kappa_850 = 0.077 m^2 kg^-1; flat LambdaCDM (H0 = 67.8 km/s/Mpc, Omega_M = 0.31, Omega_Lambda = 0.69)

recipe.goal: Derive molecular gas luminosities, dynamical masses, gas mass, gas fraction, and depletion timescale
recipe.method: Integrate reconstructed source-plane CO line cubes to get intrinsic line luminosities; compute dynamical mass from 2*R_eff and inclination-corrected maximum velocity; convert CO(3-2) luminosity of HS 0810+2554 to gas mass and depletion time
key_parameters: inclination i = 45 +/- 15 deg where axis ratio is unconstrained (RX J0911+0551, PG 1115+080, WFI J2033-4723)
assumptions: Circular velocity traces gas rotation in a disc; alpha_CO = 0.8 M_sun (K km s^-1 pc^2)^-1 for HS 0810+2554

score_reason: Raw ALMA project codes, physical equations, and numerical answer keys for all targets are clearly provided, but reproduction of the core source-plane reconstructions is blocked by the unstated availability of the specialized visibility-plane pixellated lens modelling code (Powell et al. 2020) and two missing tables (lens model parameters and spectral line setup) in the text.
rediscovery_reason: All ALMA project codes are public in the archive, lens-plane continuum fluxes and CO line Gaussian FWHMs can be directly reproduced with standard CASA scripts, and intrinsic sizes/SED properties provide well-defined numeric targets if an equivalent visibility-plane lens modelling tool (e.g. PyAutoLens or visilens) is used.
